newsitem.title: USA: US BLS seeks bigger FY98 budget for CPI changes.
newsitem.headline: US BLS seeks bigger FY98 budget for CPI changes.

text.p: The head of the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics said the agency has asked for a bigger budget for fiscal year 1998 so it can make changes to the way it calculates the consumer price index.
BLS Commissioner Katharine Abraham told the Senate Budget Committee that the White House has agreed to support the budget request, but she provided no specific dollar amounts.

Abraham said the additional funds would in part allow the BLS to improve the methods used to adjust for "quality change" by expanding the amount of information collected on the prices and characteristics of certain goods and services.
The extra money would also go toward speeding up the process of updating the CPI market basket in future revisions.

Abraham said additional resources would also be used to produce additional measures of change in consumer prices that "we believe would provide closer approximations to the change in the cost of living than the currently published CPI."

Abraham made the budget announcement at a hearing on the findings of a panel appointed by Congress to study the CPI. She reiterated BLS' disagreements with the panel over "what changes to the index would be feasible and prudent and about the timetable on which those changes could be implemented."
